suspects.description: Ghidra pre-increment-array-walk loop artifact on `pCVar2` (per-iteration advance via struct-field/pointer arithmetic — single-var `pCVar2 = pCVar2;` self-assign, two-var `tmp = &pCVar2->field; pCVar2 = tmp;` ping-pong, or a bare `pCVar2 = pCVar2 + N;` advance followed by a `*pCVar2 =` store — plus a constant-index store on `pCVar2`). Watcom's advance-then-displaced-store (`ADD reg,N` / store `[reg + -N]`) loses the displacement here, so every store lands one element late and the first is never written. The stride/sentinel are baked from the original struct layout, so it overruns on any layout change (e.g. the 64-bit port). Always wrong as-decoded; cross-reference .asm and rewrite as a straightforward for-loop in a .keep (watch for the skip-row store-offset bug).
suspects.match: do { advance(var via &field or +N); var[K]/arr[0]... store; ...}
